dish: Chōju-zen longevity set (≈15 small dishes of Yanbaru island vegetables, by reservation)
n: Emi no Mise, Ōgimi (笑味の店)
w: Opened in 1990 by Kinjō Shōko to pass on the food culture of Ōgimi, the 'longevity village'; a farm restaurant whose reservation-only chōju-zen longevity set is built on seasonal island vegetables she grows herself. Her book of Yanbaru grandmothers' kitchen wisdom was published in 2023 (Ryukyu Shimpo).

dish: Ganso beni-imo tart (purple sweet-potato tart; hand-making experience)
n: Okashi Goten Onna (御菓子御殿 恩納店)
address: Onna-son, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan (coastal Route 58; red-gated palace-style shop)
w: The red-gated seaside flagship of the confectioner behind the 'original' beni-imo tart, made from 100% Okinawan purple sweet potato from contracted farmers with no preservatives or colouring; the baking line is visible through glass and a reservation-only tart-making class runs here.

dish: Mozuku soba (homemade noodles kneaded with organic Ōjima-coast mozuku seaweed)
n: Mozuku Soba Kunnatu, Nanjō (もずくそばの店 くんなとぅ)
w: Facing Ōjima, a mozuku-farming centre, this shop kneads JAS-organic mozuku into its own soba noodles and serves them in a light bonito broth with tempura fried to order.

dish: Seaside soup (house cream soup with pork-bone broth, mushrooms and ham), to stay or take out
n: Seaside Drive-In, Onna (シーサイドドライブイン)
address: Nakadomari, Onna-son, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan (Route 58, seaside)
w: Opened in 1967 under US administration and kept in its original style, neon signs and all; the signature creamy pork-bone soup is a take-out ritual for west-coast beach days, and a 24-hour take-out counter sells burgers, shaved ice and sides.

dish: Kusu (aged awamori) tasting — cellar of decades-old jar-aged kusu
n: Yamakawa Shuzō awamori distillery, Motobu (山川酒造)
w: Motobu distillery founded in 1946 that makes awamori and long-aged kusu with Motobu spring water; cellar tours show rows of 50-year-old kusu jars and end with tastings that include 20-year-old kusu. Ryukyu Shimpo has reviewed its jar-aged 2011 vintage.

dish: Ryū awamori kusu aged in the Kin limestone cave (cave cellar tour + bottle-keep)
n: Kin Shōnyūdō cave awamori cellar — Ryū no Kura, Kin (金武鍾乳洞 古酒蔵 龍の蔵)
w: Since 1988 Kin Shuzō has aged its 'Ryū' awamori in a 270 m limestone cave held at a constant 18°C — billed as Japan's first cave kusu cellar — where over 14,000 bottles sit, many of them visitors' bottle-keeps for 5, 12 or 20 years; guided cave tours run three times a day.
